projectDetails.name: Gelato
projectDetails.description: Gelato is a Web3 automation and infrastructure protocol that enables developers to automate smart contract actions, relays transactions, and power gasless user experiences.

topRisks.content: Misconfigured user smart contracts relying on Gelato automation were abused in arbitrage strategies, causing losses to affected users; the Gelato infrastructure itself was not hacked but the incident highlighted configuration and integration risk.
The lack of a structured Bug Bounty program reduces proactive vulnerability discovery, raising the risk that attackers find issues first.
Missing CCSS certification leaves crypto custody controls unvalidated, increasing the risk of undetected security gaps.

reviews.text: Gelato is an automation hub for smart contracts. Launched in 2019, it provides bots for on-chain tasks. In 2025, it’s multi-chain with relay services.

Gelato is basically one of the few automation engines for Web3, covering around 78% of the market. It helps smart contracts to self-execute, with actions like trigger trades, harvest yield or rebalance portfolios, without needing a person to press the button. Those automations are used in DeFi tools that auto-compound or set limit orders, where there is a good chance Gelato was working in the background. It works across many chains like Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism and even zkSync. Gelato lets developers add autopilot features to their dApps. So instead of checking constantly, things can happen when conditions are met. It’s expanding, by supporting rollups, intent-based transactions and gasless experiences. It also supported the creation of Kraken's new L2 chain, INK.

Gelato to me is like a personal assistant for DeFi it lets you automate smart contract calls like swaps or liquidations without doing it manually. I find it user friendly: it even works with Flashbots to avoid front running and provides a nice interface for scheduling tasks. My concern is that its execution layer is currently permissioned tasks are run by a whitelist of nodes. It plans to decentralize, but for now you have to trust Gelato’s operators. That’s something I keep in mind when using it.

Gelato is a decentralized automation protocol that enables users to automate smart contract executions across multiple blockchains. By providing a secure and reliable way to schedule and execute transactions, Gelato enhances the functionality of decentralized applications (dApps) by allowing them to run automatically, without manual intervention. It’s particularly useful for use cases like DeFi, NFTs, and any platform that needs recurring or triggered transactions.
